title: Fractions, one piece at a time

lessons.objective: Recognise equal parts of the same whole.
Explain the numerator and denominator using a picture.
Show why different fractions can describe the same amount.
Add fractions whose pieces have the same size.
Use tenths and hundredths to write the same amount in a new way.
Read a ratio in order, distinguish a part-to-part ratio from a fraction of the whole, and scale both quantities together.

sources.name: OpenStax — Prealgebra 2e: Decimals (place value and fractions)

glossary.definition: The complete amount used as the reference.
The number of selected equal parts.
The number of equal parts making one whole.
Describing the same amount, even with different-sized pieces.
The mark separating whole-number places from tenths, hundredths and smaller places.
A comparison of two quantities in a stated order, such as juice to water.

outcomes: Recognise equal parts of the same whole.
Explain the numerator and denominator using a picture.
Show why different fractions can describe the same amount.
Add fractions whose pieces have the same size.
Compare two quantities with a ratio and scale both while preserving their proportions.
description: Seven short lessons: start with equal pieces, read and compare fractions, meet decimals, then use ratios to make a picnic drink. Optional quizzes included.
introduction:
Start with equal pieces of one whole. Learn to read, compare and add fractions, then meet decimals and use a ratio to make a bigger batch of a drink.

Read at your own pace and check the small examples. Each lesson has an optional short quiz; you can return to any chapter whenever you like.
prerequisites: Comfort with counting, addition and equal sharing. Maths from zero is a useful starting point.
